_comment: Declared derivation for this record: text.txt == extract -> slice -> reflow -> mechanical -> corrections, byte-exact against text_sha256. Verified by scripts/derive_text.py. Every human repair of an extraction defect is recorded here with a reason, so nothing about the derivation lives only in the stored bytes.

extractor._reason: The stored original is the UNOOSA treaty page captured as markdown, so no PDF extraction is involved.

slice.start_contains: ### Agreement Governing the Activities of States
slice._reason: The UNOOSA page reproduces the adopting instrument — General Assembly resolution 34/68 — with the Agreement as its ANNEX. The slice starts at the annex heading (line 388 of the capture), not the resolution title at line 357 which contains the same words; the anchor stops at 'States' because the heading reads 'States  on' with a double space.

_reflow_reason: Hard wrapping plus 25 NO-BREAK SPACE padding lines, as with the other UNOOSA captures.
_mechanical_reason: As with the sibling treaty pages, plus dehyphenate: this capture breaks compound words across lines and leaves the hyphen with a trailing space ('man- made', 'non- governmental' twice). A hyphen followed by a space between two word characters is a line-break artefact, not punctuation the Agreement contains.

corrections._reason: Article 3(4). The capture lost the 'oeu' ligature from 'manoeuvres', leaving 'man uvres' with a space where the glyph failed to render. The same class of defect as the broken glyph recorded in nat/lux. Restored to the authentic spelling used in the Agreement.

Article 18. The capture reads 'as depository'; the authentic Agreement reads 'as depositary'. These are different words in treaty practice — a depositary is the office that holds the instrument and receives ratifications — so this is a substantive restoration, not a spelling preference.

_verified.note: Two human repairs, both declared with the article they sit in. Count guards apply.
